articles.title: Steven Spielberg to make a western written by Paul Thomas Anderson
articles.summary: Jessie Buckley, Cillian Murphy and Mark Rylance will reportedly star in adaptation of The Heart in Winter. Steven Spielberg has announced his next project: a western scripted by Paul Thomas Anderson.
body: According to Deadline, the two Oscar-winning film-makers will collaborate for an adaptation of Kevin Barry’s 2024 novel The Heart in Winter.
The film is set to bring together the Oscar-winning actors Jessie Buckley, Cillian Murphy and Mark Rylance. It tells the story of two fugitives on the run in the 1890s.

“It’s really the excitement for me to get to work together with my dear friend and colleague Paul Thomas Anderson on a genre, but more particularly, the genre notwithstanding, a story that quite quickly became close to both our hearts and we felt that we could do as a team,” Spielberg told Deadline.

Earlier this year, Spielberg also spoke about the film while at SXSW. “Can’t reveal anything right now, but I have a western in development,” he said, before adding that “it kicks ass” and “there will be no tropes”.

articles.title: Focker In-Law review – triangle of sadness as Ariana Grande joins Stiller and De Niro in the circle of trust
articles.summary: Even Grande’s talent can’t save the fourth outing of this 90s-style grossout cringe comedy from a depressing sense of overfamiliarity. So to the fourth film in the most consistently moderate but undeniably lucrative comedy franchise in modern Hollywood history, often featuring heavyweight actors…
body: Even now, even after all this time, I’m still not convinced that the great Robert De Niro is 100% on top of it. He sometimes gives the impression – the same impression he’s given in the previous three movies – that he’s thinking about something else.

This started more than a quarter of a century ago, when gags about beta-males employed as nurses and called Gaylord Focker were cooler than they are today and this film is possibly the last surviving example of old-school grossout cringe comedy from the 90s era of There’s Something About Mary.

Ben Stiller was Focker himself, the nervy, prickly guy engaged to Pam (Teri Polo); he had to meet his future father-in-law, former CIA agent Jack Byrnes (De Niro) who put Gaylord through an excruciating process of assessment over a mortifying weekend, in the course of which Focker met Teri’s impossibly charismatic ex, Kevin (Owen Wilson).

articles.title: Chemicals, Covid and cabbage: why 2026 has been an amazing year for documentaries
articles.summary: With Musk, NAZA and You Can See Everything finding large audiences, non-fiction cinema is poised to break through. But there are plenty more gripping stories waiting for their turn in the spotlight.
body: There comes a time in the life of every film enthusiast when they must set aside foolish fictions and face up to some hard truths. Specifically, that time arrives each November in the form of the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA for short), with its tales of crisis and strife, angry resistance and everyday human kindness. The world’s largest documentary festival plays out in the city’s twinkling downtown district, quite near the torture museum, and provides a sharp corrective to the confected dramas and A-list pageantry of Cannes, Toronto and Venice. The forecast is bracing, stormy, and occasionally chilling. Hours of darkness; no stars.

articles.title: Designing a ‘Hunger Games’ Prequel: From Using 600,000 Flowers in the ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ Arena to Recreating the Capitol in the 1970s
articles.summary: Production designer Uli Hanisch thought shooting the highly anticipated “Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” in the remote town of Asturias, Spain, meant they would be safe from spoilers.
body: Even though sleuthing fans were able to find it, the location is so secluded that Hanisch wondered if it would be feasible to get a crew of the necessary magnitude all the way up there. But once he saw the luscious greenery contrasting the jagged mountains, he knew they had found the arena for the Second Quarter Quell, and they’d have to make it work.

The next step was designing and building the Cornucopia — the focal point of the arena, which distinguishes each iteration of the Hunger Games (and each installment of the film franchise) from the others. Similar to the paradoxical landscape, Hanisch and his team wanted to create something that balanced beauty with danger. They landed on a blossom with metal spikes for petals, surrounded by thick beds of wildflowers, arranged by color, demarking each tribute’s position around the centerpiece.

“It’s very beautiful, it’s very elegant, but it also looks very deadly and evil,” Hanisch says. “When they were shooting the opening, and the tributes were all around with these capes, I thought this looked like one of those satanic, strange cults. I thought it was actually a very matching feel.”

body: Don’t overlook the international animated titles that have demonstrated pockets of support. Japan enters the race with “Cosmic Princess Kaguya!,” “All You Need Is Kill” and “Mobile Suit Gundam Hathaway: The Sorcery of Nymph Circe,” while Mexico offers the stop-motion feature “I Am Frankelda” and Spain brings “Decorado.”

The Academy notes that some still need to complete their required theatrical runs and meet the category’s other rules before they can advance. Animation branch members vote automatically for the five nominees. Members of other branches can opt in, as long as they meet a minimum viewing requirement. Animated features can also compete in other categories, best picture included, and a country’s official international feature submission can be considered for animated feature.

articles.title: Super Bowl 2027 and Jay-Z Halftime Show to Screen in Imax Theaters
articles.summary: Can’t get a ticket to the big game? Worry not, because Imax is bringing Super Bowl LXI to the big screen. Imax is working with ESPN, the Walt Disney Company and the NFL to screen the Super Bowl in the company’s premium theaters for the first time. The game will play in hundreds of Imax
body: Super Bowl LXI will be held on Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif. Imax theater tickets are expected to go on sale in January. The four-hour presentation will feature ESPN’s main game telecast and the halftime show headlined by Jay-Z, as well as pregame and postgame coverage. A promotional spot and other marketing materials for the event will appear in theaters during Thanksgiving week. Additional details, including a list of participating locations and ticketing information, will be announced in the coming weeks.

“Watching the Super Bowl with your fellow fans is one of the great shared experiences in sports, and this first-of-its-kind collaboration with the NFL and Imax takes it to a historic new scale,” said Ken Potrock, the Walt Disney Company’s president of major event integration. “With ESPN’s first Super Bowl, we’re reaching fans across an unprecedented range of platforms and meeting them wherever they want to be, with unique moments that only Disney and ESPN can deliver.”
Rich Gelfond, CEO of Imax, called the Super Bowl programming “a milestone for Imax that further elevates our standing as a premier global platform for entertainment and events.”

articles.title: Why New Wave Music Won’t Go Away: New Documentary Explores How Synthesizers, MTV and Androgyny Built the Enduring Genre
articles.summary: From “Stranger Things” to virtually any Trader Joe’s, new wave music is inescapable. Not only are bands like B-52s, Duran Duran, Tears for Fears and Billy Idol still frequently touring, new generations are embracing the danceable sounds of 1977 to 1987, whether the tunes are making shoppers dance…
body: In the doc, musicians, DJs and veejays (Martha Quinn! Mark Goodman!) consider the ingredients that created the movement: the influence of women, the colorful and original fashions of the era and the dawn of MTV, all coming together to create a joyful decade of energetic music that still resonates today.

Interviews in the four-part series include Kate Pierson and Fred Schneider of the B52s, Billy Idol, Mark Mothersbaugh of Devo, Danny Elfman of Oingo Boingo, Stewart Copeland of the Police, John Taylor of Duran Duran, Curt Smith of Tears for Fears, Johnny Marr of the Smiths, Kathy Valentine of the Go-Gos, Brian Setzer of Stray Cats and Jim Kerr of Simple Minds.

New wave torchbearer Richard Blade, the KROQ and Sirius First Wave DJ who has helped keep fans engaged with the sound ever since it started, serves as consulting producer, with Douglas Tirola directing. R.J. Cutler and Elise Pearlstein are among the executive producers. The production company is This Machine Filmworks, a part of Sony Pictures Television.

articles.title: You Can See Everything passes $100m at global box office as UK release starts strong
articles.summary: The documentary from Nathan Fielder following fraudster Elizabeth Holmes in the weeks leading up to her imprisonment has broken box office records in the UK. Elizabeth Holmes film You Can See Everything has crossed the $100m mark at the global box office as it recorded the highest ever opening…
body: Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, You Can See Everything earned an estimated $2.5m over the weekend on its sixth week of release in North America, according to Box Office Mojo, bringing its total there to $93.5m. This has been augmented by successful releases in a number of international territories, which has added an estimated $9m for a total of $102.5m.

This means the film is already the seventh highest grossing documentary of all time, in a list currently headed by the 2009 film Michael Jackson’s This Is It on $267.9m. In North America alone, it is now the third highest grossing documentary, behind Fahrenheit 9/11 and Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour.

Despite releasing a month and a half later, the UK has seen stellar figures on the film’s first weekend in cinemas. Variety reports it took an estimated $3.2m (£2.4m) from more than 590 venues, itself a record for a non-music documentary.
You Can See Everything has proved to be a significant commercial success for its backers, which include distribution outfit A24, with the film reportedly costing $7m to make.

articles.title: US rapper postpones O2 arena show after Manchester evacuation
articles.summary: Don Toliver's show on Sunday was evacuated after an "unknown substance" was released into the crowd.
body: "I'm very sad to sit here and say I have to reschedule The O2 London show to December 15th due to (the) unfortunate incident last night," he wrote on Instagram.
One person was taken to hospital and a total of 89 people showed "symptoms believed to be linked to the exposure" after Sunday's Co-op Live arena show, police said.
Fans described "distressing scenes" with people "choking", "screaming" and "coughing up blood" because of the effects of a substance, which police initially believed to be tear gas.
Leon Douzi said he was right next to where the substance was released, explaining there was someone holding a can and "this gas coming out".

articles.title: Britain's Got Talent winner almost missed audition due to Carphone Warehouse shift
articles.summary: Tenor Paul Potts would have missed his big chance if a colleague didn't work his Saturday shift.
body: Britain's Got Talent winner Paul Potts said he nearly missed his life-changing audition on the show because he had been unable to get time off from his job managing a phone shop.

The tenor shot to fame in 2007 after performing Nessun Dorma on the ITV talent show, but had unsuccessfully tried to change the date of his performance because of his shift at Port Talbot's Carphone Warehouse.
"It was only thanks to a colleague who normally didn't work Saturdays that came into cover me – otherwise I wouldn't have been there," he said.
He has since released six albums, reached the final of America's Got Talent: The Champions and inspired the Hollywood film One Chance.

articles.title: ‘The Odyssey’ Leads Critics Choice Awards Below-The-Line Shortlists
articles.summary: The Christopher Nolan epic was recognized in 11 out of 12 categories, followed by 'Dune: Part Three' and 'La Bola Negra' with eight placements each.
body: The Critics Choice Association has announced the shortlists for the 32nd Annual Critics Choice Awards in 12 below-the-line categories: best casting and ensemble, best young actor/actress, best cinematography, best Production Design, best editing, best costume design, best hair and makeup, best visual effects, best stunt design, best song, best score and best sound.

As previously announced, Abbott Elementary star Janelle James will host the 32nd annual Critics Choice Awards being held on Sunday, Jan. 3, 2027, at The Barker Hangar in Santa Monica. The ceremony returns to E! for the third consecutive year, and to USA Network for the second, with the telecast airing live on both the East and West coasts from 7:00-10:00 p.m. ET/4:00-7:00 p.m. PT.

Nominations in both the film and television categories for the 2026 Critics Choice Awards will be announced Live on Friday, December 4 at 12:00 p.m. ET/9:00 a.m. PT on E! and USA Network as well as CriticsChoice.com.
